SeverityRuleFindingClauses
high CG001Plaintext transport across a trust boundary
Back-office clerk → Payments ledger line 19
"Edits rejected orders" crosses a trust boundary: SQL declared without TLS.
Proposed fix: Use TLS (HTTPS, JDBC/TLS, AMQPS, mTLS ...) and say so in the technology label, or add $tags="enc:tls".
 GDPR:Art32(1)(a)NIS2:2022/2555:Art21(2)(h)
high CG002External system called without declared authentication
Payment engine → Clearing ICT provider line 21
"Sends payment orders": no authentication declared (missing fact).
Proposed fix: Declare the mechanism, e.g. $tags="auth:oauth2", "auth:mtls" or "auth:managed_identity".
 NIS2:2022/2555:Art21(2)(j)GDPR:Art32
high CG003Personal-data store without declared encryption at rest
Payments ledger line 11
Holds personal data; encryption at rest is not declared (missing fact).
Proposed fix: Declare it, e.g. $tags="pii;at_rest:aes256" (or at_rest:cmk for customer-managed keys).
 GDPR:Art32(1)(a)NIS2:2022/2555:Art21(2)(h)
high CG006Database reachable directly from a person or the internet
Back-office clerk → Payments ledger line 19
"Edits rejected orders" connects Back-office clerk directly to a database.
Proposed fix: Route access through an application or API tier that authenticates and authorises; keep the database in an internal zone.
 NIS2:2024/2690:Annex-6.8GDPR:Art25
medium CG005Critical third-party ICT service without a declared exit or alternative
Clearing ICT provider line 15
Tagged critical; no exit strategy or alternative declared.
Proposed fix: Declare the exit path, e.g. $tags="critical;exit:secondary-provider", and draw the alternative if it exists.
 DORA:2022/2554:Art28(8)DORA:2022/2554:Art28NIS2:2022/2555:Art21(2)(d)
medium CG007No logging or monitoring component in a system handling personal data
whole diagram line 4
2 element(s) handle personal data; no element tagged logging.
Proposed fix: Add the log sink to the diagram and tag it, e.g. Container(logs, "Central logging", "OpenTelemetry", $tags="logging").
 NIS2:2024/2690:Annex-3.2DORA-RTS:2024/1774:Art12
medium CG008Credential-based connections without a secrets store
Payment engine → Payments ledger line 20
"Posts entries" authenticates with password; no element tagged secrets.
Proposed fix: Add a secrets store (Key Vault, Vault, KMS) tagged secrets, or switch to workload identity (auth:managed_identity, auth:mtls).
 NIS2:2022/2555:Art21(2)(i)GDPR:Art32
medium CG010Personal data sent to an external system with no declared processing region
Payment engine → Clearing ICT provider line 21
"Sends payment orders" sends personal data to Clearing ICT provider; region not declared (missing fact).
Proposed fix: Declare the location on the external system, e.g. $tags="region:eu-west", and record the transfer safeguard if it is outside the EU/EEA.
 GDPR:Art44GDPR:Art46

Clauses cited

DORA-RTS:2024/1774:Art12 Logging
Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1774 (DORA RTS on ICT risk management), Art. 12. Financial entities define and run logging procedures and tools: which events are logged, how long logs are kept and how log data is protected.
DORA:2022/2554:Art28 General principles for the management of ICT third-party risk
Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 (DORA), Art. 28. Financial entities stay responsible when they rely on ICT third-party providers and manage that risk inside their ICT risk management framework, including concentration risk.
DORA:2022/2554:Art28(8) General principles for the management of ICT third-party risk (exit strategies)
Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 (DORA), Art. 28(8). For ICT services that support critical or important functions, financial entities need exit strategies that let them leave a provider without disrupting the business.
GDPR:Art25 Data protection by design and by default
Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR), Art. 25. Controllers build appropriate technical and organisational measures into the design of processing and, by default, process only the personal data each purpose needs.
GDPR:Art32 Security of processing
Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR), Art. 32. Controllers and processors apply security measures appropriate to the risk, such as encryption, resilience, recovery and regular testing.
GDPR:Art32(1)(a) Security of processing (pseudonymisation and encryption)
Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR), Art. 32(1)(a). Pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data are named as examples of appropriate security measures.
GDPR:Art44 General principle for transfers
Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR), Art. 44. Personal data leaves the EU/EEA only under the conditions of GDPR Chapter V, so knowing where a recipient processes data matters.
GDPR:Art46 Transfers subject to appropriate safeguards
Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR), Art. 46. Without an adequacy decision, a transfer to a third country needs appropriate safeguards such as standard data protection clauses.
NIS2:2022/2555:Art21(2)(d) Cybersecurity risk-management measures (supply chain security)
Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2), Art. 21(2)(d). Risk-management measures cover supply chain security, including the relationship with direct suppliers and service providers.
NIS2:2022/2555:Art21(2)(h) Cybersecurity risk-management measures (cryptography and encryption)
Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2), Art. 21(2)(h). Risk-management measures include policies on the use of cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption.
NIS2:2022/2555:Art21(2)(i) Cybersecurity risk-management measures (access control and asset management)
Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2), Art. 21(2)(i). Risk-management measures include access control policies and asset management, which covers how credentials are held.
NIS2:2022/2555:Art21(2)(j) Cybersecurity risk-management measures (authentication and secured communications)
Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2), Art. 21(2)(j). Risk-management measures include multi-factor or continuous authentication and secured communications where appropriate.
NIS2:2024/2690:Annex-3.2 Monitoring and logging
Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690, Annex, point 3.2. In-scope entities monitor and log activity on their network and information systems, decide what is logged, review logs and keep them for a defined period.
NIS2:2024/2690:Annex-6.8 Network segmentation
Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690, Annex, point 6.8. In-scope entities segment systems into zones by risk, keep critical systems in secured zones and restrict traffic between zones to what operation needs.

c4-guardrails assesses what a design-time diagram declares against deterministic rules. It evidences gaps and proposes fixes; it is not a compliance certification and not legal advice.
